fixed_key_findings.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?
fixed_key_findings.old_fixed_key_answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated.
old_required_facts: Unqualified Power Damage normally hurts Invaders in the target land; it does not normally harm Dahan.
Damage from normal separate Powers can combine during the turn.
Damage reaching Health immediately destroys a piece; survivor Damage clears at Time Passes.
Destroying a Town/City causes 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear.
Remove/Replace themselves generate no destruction Fear.
Replace retains prior Damage and can cause destruction if it meets the new piece's Health.
fixed_key_findings.recommended_correction: Explicitly distinguish direct Destroy and Remove from Damage: a direct Destroy instruction eliminates its specified Invader regardless of its remaining Health or Damage; Remove also takes the specified piece off the board without a Damage/Health test, but does not generate destruction Fear. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place, retaining marked Damage, with a new Health check on the replacement. Do not require a second recital of actor or removal details when the answer already states these results unambiguously.
fixed_key_findings.reason: Q18 expressly asks how all four operations differ for survival, as well as Fear. The key/map state the Damage threshold and replacement retention, but the Destroy/Remove clauses cover only Fear. An answer following those listed requirements could omit the asked distinction between damage requiring sufficient Damage and an outright Destroy/Remove bypassing that test. This is an answer-scope omission; none of the existing quoted key facts is false.

primary_sources.anchor: CORE p18: removal, replacement, outright destruction versus Damage/Health
CORE p15: some effects destroy Invaders regardless of Damage or Health

remaining_gaps.topic: Health-based removal uses modified current Health
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: An effect permits removing 3 Health worth of Invaders. A healthy Town currently has 3 Health because of an already-active Health modifier. Does removing that Town spend 2 or 3 of the allowance? Does marked Damage change the allowance spent?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: It spends 3: use current Health including Health modifiers. Damage is a separate total and does not lower that Health or the removal allowance spent.

primary_sources.anchor: FAQ .9v5kaai: Health-based removals consider all current Health modifiers, not marked Damage

remaining_gaps.actual_prompt_overlap_assessment: Q52 asks whether two Cities may be removed and whether marked Damage reduces Health. Its map explicitly treats modifier handling as unasked context. Q92 asks batching/pooling. Q143 instead tests Ocean's exceptional printed-Health exchange. None requests the ordinary modified-Health removal valuation. The Damage clause above is disclosed overlap with Q52.
remaining_gaps.why_novel: A distinct resource-allowance valuation rule: ignoring modifiers produces a different permitted removal set. This is not a new numerical card payload; the modifier is a stated generic condition, with no excluded producer.
remaining_gaps.scope_assessment: INCLUDED: standard original-core procedure or applicable generic official clarification. No expansion, promo, Adversary, Scenario or thematic-board producer is introduced.

remaining_gaps.topic: Each-player Fear instructions finish before the next player starts
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: A Fear Card tells each player to Gather a Dahan and then deal Damage in the chosen land. May player A Gather, player B Gather, and then both deal their Damage, or must one player finish that player's full instruction before the next begins?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: One player follows that player's instructions fully, then the next player does. Do not interleave the two players' instruction sequences.

primary_sources.anchor: CORE p9 EACH PLAYER sidebar: first one player follows instructions fully, then next

remaining_gaps.actual_prompt_overlap_assessment: Q12 asks new-card timing/Terror and own-Presence restrictions; its map expressly excludes complete-player execution from required facts. Q51 permits successive choices to reuse pieces; Q99 defines the action units for outcome checks. Neither asks whether instructions within those per-player units may be interleaved. Q05 prohibits one Power interrupting another, rather than explaining multi-player Fear execution.
remaining_gaps.why_novel: An explicit temporal execution rule for each-player Fear effects; interleaving can change both pieces and Damage counts. It is distinct from where choices may occur and from how action units are counted.
remaining_gaps.scope_assessment: INCLUDED: standard original-core procedure or applicable generic official clarification. No expansion, promo, Adversary, Scenario or thematic-board producer is introduced.

remaining_gaps.proposed_question: After a primary action and all triggered actions finish, an Invader is still illegally placed. Do players check victory/defeat with that illegal position first, or correct its position before that check? Assume a legal destination exists.
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Correct the illegal position first, after the action tree and immediately before checking victory/defeat. Apply the normal cleanup to the nearest legal land, then evaluate the resulting state.

primary_sources.anchor: FAQ .7w4gdtl: cleanup after each action tree, just before victory/defeat

remaining_gaps.actual_prompt_overlap_assessment: Q81 asks how cleanup works and its classification; the map explicitly places its outcome-check timing in context. Q100 also excludes that timing. Q20/Q46/Q103 require complete action trees before outcome checks, but do not place the separate non-action cleanup before that check.
remaining_gaps.why_novel: A source-defined timing boundary between two different procedures. It determines the state on which victory/defeat is assessed; it cannot be established merely by a key sentence that the prompt did not request.
remaining_gaps.scope_assessment: INCLUDED: standard original-core procedure or applicable generic official clarification. No expansion, promo, Adversary, Scenario or thematic-board producer is introduced.

remaining_gaps.topic: Attribute-changing thresholds are checked before affected attribute checks
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: A Power has a threshold that increases its Range or changes its Speed. When is that threshold applied: before checking the applicable Range/Speed, or only at its printed position after the base effects? Can an Element gained by a base instruction retroactively make an earlier invalid target or phase valid?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Apply the attribute-modifying threshold when checking the affected Speed, Range or targeting, before the normal effects as necessary. A later Element gain may qualify later ordinary thresholds, but cannot retroactively repair a previously invalid Speed/Range/target check or revise completed effects.

primary_sources.anchor: FAQ .9v5kcmx: Speed/Range thresholds checked first
FAQ .bu6od0c footnote2: Speed/Range/targeting effects apply at their attribute check

remaining_gaps.actual_prompt_overlap_assessment: Q27 asks whether new/lost Elements change later thresholds and whether earlier effects may be revised; its map explicitly excludes attribute-modifier prechecks. Q106 assumes an internal Range threshold and asks persistence/nonstacking on Repeat. Q133 asks the different printed First/Before exception. No literal prompt asks when to apply a Speed/Range/targeting threshold.
remaining_gaps.why_novel: A source-defined exception to ordinary printed order. The non-retroactivity part overlaps Q27, but applying a threshold before choosing/checking a target or phase is an additional temporal procedure.
remaining_gaps.scope_assessment: INCLUDED: standard original-core procedure or applicable generic official clarification. No expansion, promo, Adversary, Scenario or thematic-board producer is introduced.

remaining_gaps.topic: Immediate triggered Repeat can use a just-Forgotten card
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: Call on Midnight's Dream is used and Forgotten for its Major gain. Assume this use also triggers an explicit permission to Repeat that same Power immediately after the use, rather than a once-this-turn option. Can that immediate Repeat occur, and can the already-Forgotten original be Forgotten again for its conditional benefit?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Yes, the immediately triggered Repeat may occur despite the card already having been Forgotten. It cannot be Forgotten again, so it cannot provide the conditional Energy gain and permission to play the second new Major through another Forget.

primary_sources.anchor: FAQ .9v5ka8w changed ruling: immediate triggered Repeat exception to Forgotten-card restriction

remaining_gaps.topic: Delayed Power trigger keeps its originating Spirit as source
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: Bringer has used Vengeance of the Dead in a land. A later action by another Spirit actually destroys a Town there, causing Bringer's Vengeance to trigger. Is the triggered Damage real because the other Spirit caused the trigger, or does it still follow To Dream a Thousand Deaths?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: The triggered Damage is still from Bringer's Power and follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths: it is hypothetical Damage, with nightmare Fear/Push if it would destroy an eligible Invader. The Spirit or action that caused the trigger does not take ownership of Bringer's triggered Power effect.

remaining_gaps.topic: Choke the Land with Green pays separately for each prevented action
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: Assume the same land would legally Build twice this turn, and Rampant Green can use Choke the Land with Green for both. Does sacrificing Presence to skip the first Build also skip the second, or must Green make a fresh decision and sacrifice Presence again?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Make a fresh choice for each Build. Skipping both requires the appropriate separate Presence sacrifice for each; the first use does not create a blanket skip for the rest of the turn.

remaining_gaps.topic: Sworn to Victory may destroy nearby Presence outside the ravaged land
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: A Ravage destroys a Dahan. Thunderspeaker has no Presence in the ravaged land but has its own Presence in an adjacent land. Can Sworn to Victory require destruction of that nearby Presence, or is the rule confined to Presence in the ravaged land?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: It can require the nearby Presence: for each Dahan destroyed in the Ravage, destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range1 of that Ravage land as instructed, not only Presence in the land itself. Resolve it after the whole Ravage.

remaining_gaps.topic: Competing Dahan attack-timing modifiers are ordered by choice
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: Assume two already-active effects modify the same Dahan's Ravage attack timing: one sets it simultaneous with Invaders and another makes it earlier. Which timing modification takes precedence? If one effect also changes Damage amount, does overwriting its timing erase that separate Damage change?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Players choose the order of the timing modifications, so the later-applied timing change determines the resulting timing. Overwriting timing does not erase other parts of either effect, such as a Damage reduction. Each Dahan still attacks only once.

primary_sources.anchor: FAQ multiple-changes-to-dahan-counterattack-timing: choice of ordering, non-timing parts preserved

remaining_gaps.why_novel: An explicit conflict-resolution permission and partial-overwrite boundary. The premise stipulates generic active modifiers without introducing Warn of Impending Conflict or an Event producer. The once-only clause is disclosed overlap with Q98.
remaining_gaps.scope_assessment: INCLUDED: standard original-core procedure or applicable generic official clarification. No expansion, promo, Adversary, Scenario or thematic-board producer is introduced.
